cues.text: As all agree, petitioner Michael Lairy’s prison sentence for unlawful handgun possession was five years longer than the applicable statutory maximum.

When Lairy filed a motion under Section twenty-two fifty-five of Title twenty-eight seeking relief from that sentence, however, the Government argued, and the courts below held, that Lairy’s Section twenty-two fifty-five motion was untimely.
As the Government now informs this Court, its decision to invoke that statute-of-limitations defense below was an “inadvertent” error.

The Government represents that it has a policy of waiving such defenses in cases involving “undisputed legal ineligibility for an enhanced noncapital sentence—that is, a sentence above the applicable statutory maximum.”
Thus, it promised to “correct its oversight by waiving the limitations defense in district court.”
Shortly thereafter, the District Court granted Lairy’s Section twenty-two fifty-five motion and released him.
In light of the Government’s policy, and the fact that Lairy has now received all the relief he requested in his Section twenty-two fifty-five motion, I concur in the denial of certiorari.
